Hey, all. I just finished Shoujo Kakumei Utena and it has instantly become one of my favorites. This is a very deep and meaningful show that's a lot of fun to deconstruct. Has a pretty powerful message about the nature of idealism and adulthood, as well. Below, I'll have my final interpretations of the show, and I'd love to hear anyone else's opinions. There'll be heavy spoilers for the entire show, so beware. If you want to read my thoughts on the first two thirds of the show, they are here and here. I'll be posting a recommendation thread later, as well, for anyone who doesn't want spoilers, but still wants to hear my pitch.

CAUTION: Utena spoilers beyond this point!

Shoujo Kakumei Utena is an exemplary illustration of the struggle of young people to find something eternal, and ultimately learning that compromise is an absolute on the road to adulthood.

Throughout the series, Tenjou Utena aspired to be a prince. The source of this goal is a prince that saved her from despair at the death of her parents when she was young. At that time, the Prince showed her something eternal; an ideal to emulate. As she grew, her identity was that of a prince, and she tried to exemplify it in the most absolute way possible, despite the fact that she is a woman. Utena's strong belief in princeliness was tested by the hopes and cynicisms of others. She fought many duels with Himemiya Anthy at her side.

Anthy, the Rose Bride, represents Utena's dream. She is the means by which Utena strives for her goal. Many people challenged Utena in order to take that dream from her and make it their own. The Black Rose Society even wished to kill Anthy and replace her with their own dream. However, Utena's solid belief in her ideal won out over all others.

The end goal of the duels is to bring about one's revolution. In other words, by winning all of the duels, one could make their ideal a truth of the world. Through this, one could ascend into adulthood because they have a strong sense of who they are and how the world works; they have something eternal to grasp on to. Mikage (Prof. Nemuro) symbolizes how one can become stuck in youth by not accepting that their ideal is not compatible with the world. Mikage fought in order to give eternal life to someone who was already dead. In the end, he found that the image he held in his mind was nothing like what the real person had been. Thus, his ideal could not be realized because it did not exist.

While Mikage was cynical and Utena was hopeful, both were naïve. They both believed that their eternal ideals could be put into place in a perfect form. Both Mikage and Utena were inspired by their idyllic memories, which proved unreliable. Neither realized that compromises have to be made on the road to adulthood.

Every young person is on the road to adulthood. The cars that carry them are driven by their strong beliefs about the world and their senses of self. In a way, our ideas about how the world works set us on different paths, but they all lead to the same destination. Some, like Mikage, want something sturdy to hold onto through this journey. Others learn that compromise is necessary to make the ascent. One of the many compromises we all make in order to come into the adult world is the loss of our innocence, which many of the Duelists committed in order to challenge Utena once again. Utena, however, retained her purity, for a time.

That is, until she fell in love with Akio. Utena's affair with Akio represents the erosion of her belief. Rather than hold out for a perfect prince to come for her, she gave in to her natural desires and gave herself to Akio. None of the men that Utena thought may be her Prince, including Akio, were embodiments of the Prince that she believed in. In essence, Utena was realizing that the Prince may not exist, and she settled for the imperfect men in front of her. Utena was so wavered by this event that she even began to forget the Prince.

Here, we come to the act of facing reality. Utena's ideal was being dissolved, but it had not died completely. Deep down, she still believed in the Prince. This can be seen through her interactions with Anthy in which she is torn between her love for Akio and Himemiya. In her final battle, we find out that the Prince never existed. Anthy knew this, but did not tell Utena because she thought that it was her lot for her heroes to fail and for her to take the blame.

This part is representative of the uncompromising nature of the young, and their swiftness in turning on those that they once believed to be their heroes. The reason that Anthy took the attack, rather than Utena, was because the masses believed that it was the dream's fault for misleading the hero. However, the hero was blind and did not realize that the ideal she was aspiring to did not exist. When Utena used the last of her strength to defend the dream, Anthy, the people turned on her and erased her from their pantheon. In the end, Utena accepted that she could not become a prince because nobody was capable of being completely perfect. Through this, she became an adult and left the school. Duly, the school forgot about her and turned its attention to new heroes in a vain attempt to find something eternal.

That concludes my thoughts on Shoujo Kakumei Utena. There was a lot of symbolism that I either couldn't grasp or didn't have the patience to add in. If I'd covered everything I had in my notes, this post would have tripled in length. Some notable suff I'd like to tack on: Utena's battle with End of the World symbolizes the need for an ideal to be destroyed before it can be replaced. Also, Akio's being at the school shows that he still believes that the Prince can be recovered and he can become that again. I couldn't quite grasp the meaning behind Anthy leaving the school in search of Utena, but I have a feeling that it's representative of Utena's dream crossing over into adulthood along with her because it is not necessary to leave all of one's beliefs behind in childhood. Finally, Utena was also hurting Anthy by posturing herself as something eternal, when no such eternity existed. Her doing so put Anthy on the chopping block later when Utena inevitably failed in being a prince.
